extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, and readers interested in publication ethics and retractions
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practices for handling image-manipulation allegations and issuing retraction notices in scientific journals, including COPE guidance and journal procedures such as pre-review figure screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image manipulation/duplication as grounds for retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles were retracted for image manipulation and overlap; anonymous reader raised concerns about manipulated or duplicated images, with the journal’s editor in chief determining a retraction was warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication detection of manipulated or duplicated images is legitimate grounds for retraction. Allegations from readers (including anonymous reports) should be investigated and can lead to retraction when manipulation or overlap is confirmed. Example: eight papers in Journal of Chemical Neuroanatomy retracted for these reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should be linked to the retracted article wherever possible
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notices of retraction should: Be linked to the retracted article wherever possible (ie, in all online versions).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link the retraction notice directly to the original article in all online versions so readers encountering the article see the retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should clearly identify the retracted article (title and authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notices of retraction should: Clearly identify the retracted article (eg, by including the title and authors in the retraction heading or citing the retracted article).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full bibliographic identification (title, authors, citation) in the retraction heading or body to avoid ambiguity about which item is retracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices must be clearly identified as retractions (distinct from corrections/comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notices of retraction should: Be clearly identified as a retraction (ie, distinct from other types of correction or comment).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish a distinct retraction notice rather than burying retraction information inside other correction formats; make the status unambiguous to readers and indexing services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should be published promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notices of retraction should: Be published promptly to minimise harmful effects.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimize delay between confirmation of a serious problem (e.g., image manipulation) and publication of the retraction to reduce ongoing harm from the faulty record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should be freely available to all readers
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notices of retraction should: Be freely available to all readers (ie, not behind access barriers or available only to subscribers).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make retraction notices open access so that anyone who encounters the original work can discover the retraction regardless of subscription status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should state who is retracting the article
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notices of retraction should: State who is retracting the article.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly indicate whether the authors, editors, publisher, or another party is issuing the retraction to clarify responsibility and provenance of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should state the reason(s) for retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notices of retraction should: State the reason(s) for retraction.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a factual explanation for the retraction (e.g., image manipulation, duplicate publication, data fabrication) so readers understand the nature of the problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction notices should be objective, factual and avoid inflammatory language
rubrics_metrics.description: “Notices of retraction should: Be objective, factual and avoid inflammatory language.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use neutral, evidence-based phrasing in retraction notices; avoid editorializing, speculation, or accusatory wording beyond what can be supported by the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue separate retraction notices to avoid confusion or stealth retractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenter recommendation: issue separate notices from the original papers to prevent confusion/false accusations of stealth retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish standalone retraction notices distinct from the original articles (and not hidden in other updates) to prevent misunderstanding and to maintain a clear record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-review screening of figures for manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher statement: “the journal will now analyze every figure before a submission is sent out to review.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement routine pre-peer-review checks (image-forensics screening) of all figures on submitted manuscripts to detect manipulation before peer review and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider correction (image replacement) vs retraction depending on severity and fixability
rubrics_metrics.description: Some authors argued replacing the images instead of retracting the paper would have been a better decision; an editor reportedly offered opportunity to resubmit if image problems were solved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the image problem is an honest, fixable error (e.g., formatting/resizing artifacts) that can be corrected with replacement or whether the problem undermines the integrity of the results and requires retraction. Offer authors chance to correct when appropriate and document the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors should investigate allegations raised by readers and determine appropriate action
rubrics_metrics.description: An anonymous reader alerted the journal; the editor-in-chief determined a retraction was warranted after investigation and correspondence with authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take reader reports seriously, investigate promptly (contact authors, examine original data/figures), and make transparent editorial decisions (correction, retraction, or other notices) based on the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retractions and editorial actions affect researcher reputations and should consider context (e.g., geographic/income disparities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors reported concerns that harsh retractions may disproportionately discourage early-career researchers from lower-income regions; debate exists about proportionality of editorial responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining remedies, consider proportionality and fairness, including whether errors arose from honest mistakes, third-party lab work, or lack of resources/training; explain rationale in the notice while maintaining factual clarity.
